items.title: Radiologists, LLMs fail at spotting AI-generated chest x-rays
items.excerpt: Seoul National University Hospital tested radiologists and LLMs on 40 real and 120 synthetic chest x-rays; neither was reliable enough to be the primary safeguard, so the authors urge cryptographic credentials or watermarking to guard image authenticity.

items.title: AI leads to lower turnaround times for high-volume imaging
items.excerpt: A JACR study of multi-vendor radiology AI at scale found report turnaround fell up to 26% for trauma imaging, worth about 0.69 radiologist FTE, but data-routing latency often decided whether AI results reached radiologists in time.

items.title: HPI: Evidence contradicts broad claims about AI, radiology workforce
items.excerpt: The Neiman Health Policy Institute rebuts a JAMA Health Forum claim that AI has reduced the need for radiologists, citing imaging demand projected to grow 17-27% by 2055 and rising radiologist workload.

items.title: Researchers develop way of adapting adult radiology AI models to pediatric population
items.excerpt: Only about 17% of FDA-authorized AI devices are labeled for children; a Nature Biomedical Engineering piece describes adapting an adult chest X-ray model to pediatrics with multi-hospital federated data that never leaves each institution. (Check vs 10-14 neonatal ETT continual-learning card - possibly same paper family.)

items.title: 미 소아 자폐 진단 AI 승인 (Argus Cognitive 'Neurora' FDA)
items.excerpt: 아거스 코그니티브의 AI 소프트웨어 '뉴로라'가 18개월~12세 자폐 스펙트럼 장애 진단 보조용 2등급 SaMD로 FDA 승인을 받았다. 업로드한 영상·음성에서 음성·얼굴·시선 등 100여 지표로 행동을 측정해 의사 판단을 보조한다.

items.title: 당뇨병학회, 진료지침 기반 AI 챗봇 개발·입원환자 CGM 도입 추진
items.excerpt: 대한당뇨병학회가 최신 진료지침을 기반으로 한 의료진용 AI 챗봇 개발과 입원환자 연속혈당측정기(CGM) 도입을 추진한다고 밝혔다.

items.title: AI가 바꾸는 진단검사의학의 미래...LMCE 10주년서 발전 방향 논의
items.excerpt: LMCE 10주년 학술대회에서 국내외 진단검사의학 전문가들이 AI를 기술 도입을 넘어 실제 검사실 진료에 적용하는 방향을 논의했다.

items.title: 임상시험도 'AI 에이전트' 시대…통합 플랫폼 경쟁 본격화
items.excerpt: EDC·CTMS 개별 전산화를 넘어 시험기관 선정부터 환자 등록, 데이터 검토, 규제 대응까지 하나로 잇는 에이전틱 AI 임상시험 플랫폼 경쟁이 본격화되고 있다.

items.title: AMA releases governance framework for agentic AI in healthcare
items.excerpt: The American Medical Association released a governance framework for AI agents in healthcare, as industry groups issue guidance on agentic AI in the absence of federal regulation.

items.title: OpenEvidence drew 271M queries from 952,000 clinicians in 2.5 years (JAMA study)
items.excerpt: A JAMA cross-sectional study (doi 10.1001/jama.2026.21868, online 2026-10-15) characterizes clinician use of the AI clinical information platform OpenEvidence: 271M queries from about 952,000 clinicians, by clinician type, specialty and query purpose. Primary source is jamanetwork.com (Cloudflare-blocked).

items.title: UChicago Medicine's CMIO: Promising 30% readmissions dip? Prove it
items.excerpt: UChicago Medicine's CMIO says AI vendors must commit to measurable outcomes such as readmission reductions and build into existing infrastructure instead of shipping point solutions.

items.title: Announcing JAMA AI - A New Journal From the JAMA Network
items.excerpt: JAMA AI, the 14th JAMA Network journal, launches in early 2027 to publish clinical research on AI and computational tools - wearables, digital pathology, imaging and implementation methods - applied to patient care. (Date verified via Crossref created; page Cloudflare-blocked.)

items.title: Public Perceptions of Timeliness for AI Use and Human Oversight
items.excerpt: Cross-sectional study of public views on AI for patient-portal messaging and mental health support, stratified by generation, with an invited commentary 'Waiting for the Human in the Loop' on timely access vs human oversight. (Crossref created 2026-10-14; canonical DOI https://doi.org/10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2026.39048.)

items.title: An AI framework for end-to-end rare disease phenotyping from clinical notes using large language models
items.excerpt: An LLM-based framework operationalizes the full rare disease phenotyping pipeline from clinical notes, replacing labor-intensive manual curation of structured phenotypes used in rare disease diagnosis.

items.title: AI-based hourly prediction of emergency department demand integrating social determinants of health
items.excerpt: An AI model forecasts hourly ED arrivals using social determinants of health alongside temporal and weather signals, aiming at proactive ED staffing against crowding linked to delayed treatment and mortality.

items.title: Early prediction of prolonged ICU stay in sepsis patients using an explainable hybrid deep learning model
items.excerpt: An explainable hybrid deep learning model predicts prolonged ICU stay early in sepsis patients, where existing severity scores fall short.

items.title: AI will force doctors to focus on clinical reasoning, experts say
items.excerpt: At an Endpoints panel, UCI Health's Pandita and Beth Israel's Rodman debated how AI tools like OpenEvidence are reshaping physician skills toward clinical reasoning.

items.title: Why Agentic AI Works in Hospitals When You Strip It Down
items.excerpt: Hospitals running many simultaneous AI-agent pilots hit 'pilot sprawl' where they cannot say which agents are still in use; the piece argues for narrow, stripped-down agent deployments. (Opinion.)

items.title: 'AI sandboxes' are all the rage. Advocates scramble to control their future
items.excerpt: STAT Health Tech newsletter: a behind-the-scenes look at groups vying to shape rules for state health-AI regulatory sandboxes. (STAT+; overlaps Utah sandbox / FSMB coverage.)

items.title: Why this startup is taking its AI to predict breast cancer risk directly to patients
items.excerpt: Clairity, maker of an FDA-authorized mammogram-based breast cancer risk prediction AI, is taking the tool direct to consumers. (STAT+; breast imaging is saturated in recent cards.)

items.title: Are Med Students Cheating if They Use AI?
items.excerpt: At the AHCJ Fall Summit, Cedars-Sinai's Graciela Gonzalez-Hernandez argued AI use in medical school is not plagiarism and described an AI-friendly curriculum that teaches prompt construction.

items.title: No Mastery without the Machine - Medical Education in the Age of Clinical AI
items.excerpt: NEJM AI perspective on how medical education must change so trainees master clinical AI tools. (Date from Crossref created.)
